Hacknet is a very fun and very realistic (I assume, I wouldn't know :D) hacking game. I got this game in a recent HumbleBundle and didn't expect to play it as it looked far too technical for me. I was worried the learning curve would be far too steep for someone like myself with no technical background whatsoever, but I was very wrong! The game is approachable and progresses you slowly enough that you can figure everything out, while not so slowly that once you're better at hacking it drags. It has the perfect pacing.

The visual and sound aesthetics are really nice in this game as well. A bit into the game you end up obtaining a software to even change the appearance of your hacking terminal (or whatever the hell the UI is called). Plenty of options for customizing to a color of your choice, it's really excellent.

All in all, this game has been a pure delight to play, even with the occasional difficulties I've had progressing. If you get stuck, there are lots of very friendly steam community threads with instructions and tips to help you move along. 8/10

This game is great. There are a few lookalikes in the store and some of them are pretty good but Hacknet is the best so far. Do yourself a favor and pick up the Labyrinths DLC as it's about the same length as the main game and introduces new mechanics on top. The overall narrative in the DLC is also a little more interesting than in the main game.

The actual hacking of systems becomes mechanical and sort of tedious after a while, and the net map gets really hard to navigate, but the former is not a big enough issue to detract from the fun of exploration / exploitation and the latter can be partially solved with some (in-game) software you'll find in your adventures.

Extra points for a perfect soundtrack!

Amazing and challenging concept. The combination of serious/humorous missions as well as the ability to mess around make the game fun even after the main story is complete.

I got this game in a recent Humble Bundle and I figured that this would just be a cute game that would entertain me for 2-3 hours tops, but i was in for a nice suprise. For example, some guy hacked my computer and screwed with my system files, so when I got access back, I tracked him down, deleted every assignment in his "/Uni" folder, then I wiped his system files for good measure. After some time passed, I got an email from a particularly angry user accusing me of deleting his school work. There are also different events that make me take a step back and really made me feel emotional. After completing Hacknet and it's Labirynths expansion I believe that the game is worth experiencing for the price it asks.

The Good:
- 8h campaign (I did some NOT ALL side missions and the Labirynth expansion)
- Interesting storylines
- Moral Disconnect/Dilemmas
- Simplicity                                   < Easy to understand, just a bit hard to remember commands etc.
- Workshop Support                     < People made some very awesome mods.
- Visuals                                        < It makes your screen look suspicious

The Bad:
- Simplicity
- Slightly difficult to navigate "network map" < Yes I am aware of the existence of the sorter. I still think it could be better in some way.

My wishlist:
- More complexity in the puzzles.
- Clearer more understandable map.
- More ways to solve objectives.
- Hardware Customisation.

Conclusion:
A very pleasant experience with possible extension via the mods on the workshop. Decent story with some interesting twists. The hacking gameplay becomes quite repetitive with time, as it just requires you to think what tool to use for each port. The investigative gameplay is actually surprisingly fun, the game leaves you with enough hints to go on, however the game rarely offers a situation to decide the outcome or change the approach to completing objective. In a certain sense it is linear.
The game that convinced me I should always try all the games I get in a Humble Bundle at least once

After playing a game like Mainlining, I felt i had a love for a new genre of game but that game specifically just didn't satisfy me enough, it was wayyy to easy. I needed to know what the next level up from there was. After looking around a bit I found several other Hacker-esk types of games but only 2 specifically called out to me, Uplink and Hacknet. While it seems definitively that Uplink is the top dog in this genres arena, I gotta admit i didn't want to step into something that might be too overwhelming for me, so I went with Hacknet; the game people say is its spiritual sequel.

Having played this game now on my 3rd play through 35hrs in(pre dlc) i gotta say i think im in love. This game just feels right in a lot of places as to what you would want from a game like this.

The story while Is short and leaves some questions unanswered. It definitely makes you feel like you are part of its world for the most part. The fact that the world is open enough to have hidden crevices/coves of information to find behind hacked emails and encrypted documents, well outside of whatever story or mission you are focused on is more than enough to feel like this is a fun sandbox to play in.

The Interface is pretty much the only graphics you get but even so it does the job. And since you can change the theme/layout later in the game, the preference is on you, they all look great to me though.

The Music is amazing (some of it feels as good as a Hotline Miami soundtrack), it's sometimes perfectly in the foreground at times syncing to what you have to deal with at the moment and other times its just softly in the background letting you focus on what you need to do next.

This game is so simple but ingenious once you dive into it. I would recommend anyone that don't mind a bit of reading and some critical thinking puzzles pick this up.

My background in computers is limited to a little tinkering in bash, so I was familiar with how command lines work and a few of the game's basic commands before I started. There might be a bit of a learning curve if you don't know what I did, but since most of the stuff can be done with a mouse instead of a keyboard, and the tutorial is thorough, it's pretty easy to pick up. On to the review:

This game is so, so good.
The gameplay, if you can call it that, consists of two parts: breaking into systems and exploring them. Breaking in is intense. You'll find yourself panicking as you type out commands as fast as you can in order to beat the trace, and when you just barely make it, you'll sigh in relief and wipe sweat off the palms of your hands. Even though it's just text and a little GUI (graphic user interface), it reels you in like nothing else.
The exploring is actually my favourite part of the game, because the game rewards your curiosity with humour, story, and extra servers and .exe's. A large portion of this game can easily be missed if you're not looking, so LOOK EVERYWHERE. If you see an IP address, it'll lead to something. Most servers have chat logs, which don't serve any gameplay purpose, but are usually hilarious. Some of the servers can even be reached before the story gives them to you, which doesn't spoil the story so much as give you this satisfaction from going where you're not supposed to go.
And that's the real magic of Hacknet: it makes you think like a hacker. There's no real hand-holding, so it's up to you to figure out what to do. You have a set of tools and a bunch of servers to mess with, and from there, you just do whatever you want. Try to go where it seems you're not supposed to, because that's exactly what hacking is. The game gets out of your way and lets you hack, which is why it doesn't feel like a game at all.

Pros:
+ Breaking into stuff is intense and rewarding
+ Exploring is fun and rewarding
+ Simple enough to be accessible to scrubs like me
+ Complex enough to make you feel like a badass hacker
+ Soundtrack is good enough that I don't feel a need to turn the volume down

Cons:
- To get the most out of the game, you need basic familiarity with a command-line interface

P.S. Play through the game in one stretch. Don't put it down for very long or you'll forget where everything is.

Abstracting real world mechanics into a video game, be it sports to hacking, is often a tricky balance between realism and fun.  'Hacknet' manages to land in the sweet spot to make it's hacking simulacrum feel like hacking while making the experience smooth enough to be enjoyable and faster paced.

The dystopian narrative also works well with the mechanics and ties in tightly with the 'who do you trust?' and 'unreliable narrator' themes common to hacking mythos.

I really enjoyed this game. The puzzles were fun and challenging and some of the mini-plots were hilarious. While the end missions seemed a little bolted on, it was well worth it.

The only issue I had was understanding how shell overload worked. I was button mashing overload and would eventually get connected, but I didn't figure out the deliberate process. After a few hours I figured it out: when a server is protected with a proxy, each press of the shell overload will increase the speed of a bar that overlays the proxy status text. If you have more shells and press more overloads, that bar goes faster. Once it is full, the proxy is bypassed.

I can imagine that this is not a game for everybody. You are terminal hacking, running programs, erasing logs, and figuring out vectors into target systems. But if you have some Linux experience and you want a hacker-esque game that gives you some thrills and chills, this is well worth it!

Hands down this is my all time favourite Hacking sim game to come out.

The terminal based commands range from realistic to semi-realistic and the sense of dread from being caught is all too real. The punishment for being detected breaking into a network involves having to hack your ISP and change the IP address they assign to you to evade being traced.

The hacking tools to open the vulnerable ports on each system are enjoyable to use and manage in regards to how much RAM you are using on your lightweight OS. 

The twists and turns in the story are absolutely thrilling along with a huge finale ending with an amazing song of choice for such an event.

The soundtrack is also amazing, cool calming atmosphere contrasting with thumping powerful tracks for those tense moments. HOME and Carpenter Brut even feature in the game and in the Labyrinths DLC.

------------------------------------------------------------
D L C
------------------------------------------------------------

Labyrinths in its own right is just as fantastic as the base game, with a brilliant storyline in this side standalone area of the game and a very tense climax at the end of it as everything comes to a head (once again featuring wonderful tracks from some of my very favourite artists)
